entry.title: Who Knew First
entry.summary: An op-ed and the record behind it. By the record's account, the organization that ran the model held the decisive facts in each of nine AI agent incidents from 2026, and in six of them someone else told the public first.

entry.title: What the Label Changes
entry.summary: A label can change where people look and how easily they make sense of an artwork, without raising liking, learning, accuracy or artistic value.

entry.title: The Second Hearing
entry.summary: Repeated listening changes liking, prediction, attention and memory in different ways. A replay count records exposure and says nothing about quality.

entry.title: The Sandbox Was Never Just a Box
entry.summary: Separate security reports expose a shared question: what can an agent reach, and can the instruments that record its actions remain trustworthy?

entry.title: LTJ Bukem: The Man Behind the Atmosphere
entry.summary: Danny Williamson’s calm, spacious records come out of a series of musical decisions, shaped by his taste and working habits and by the musicians around him.

entry.title: Borrowed Ground
entry.summary: On existence and what our work owes other people.

entry.title: Frontier Safety briefing
entry.summary: A dated monitor of AISI, Anthropic, OpenAI and industry safety records. Each edition keeps reported facts, source roles and limits apart.

entry.title: An open letter on checking the machines
entry.summary: A signed letter to the people who build AI systems: a person should be able to question a machine's answer without first winning an argument with its owner.

entry.title: A witness should not become a ruler
entry.summary: An expanded essay on the public tool portfolio, contribution from outside academia, evidence for review and changing educational practice.

entry.title: Growth Needs a Before
entry.summary: Feeling changed after trauma can matter on its own. Measuring lasting change asks for a before, an after, and clear limits on what the score can prove.

entry.title: Availability Is Not Reach
entry.summary: Tutoring has strong trial evidence. Public claims about a program must keep its availability, reach, dosage, staffing and outcomes as separate facts.

entry.title: Five evidence lanes, one OpenAI and Hugging Face incident
entry.summary: Separate legal process, OpenAI's company report, Hugging Face host telemetry, independent analysis, and vendor remediation before drawing conclusions from the July incident.
